# Phase 3 — Final Brainstorm

The Awtsmoos recreates every boundary from nothing; the final brainstorm joins routing, runtime, API, CSS, tests, Git, and deployment into one witnessed flow.
Awtsmoos.com must not merely look repaired. It must expose enough evidence that another developer can repeat the proof.

## Final System Shape

### 1. Establish Reality

Capture Git identity, branch, remotes, HEAD, working tree, active server processes, ports, package scripts, and deployment configuration. Classify concurrent/unrelated changes without erasing them.

### 2. Reproduce The Visible Failure

Open `/apps` through the actual local server. Capture console, failed requests, module URLs, redirect chains, response headers, and final bodies. Separate extension noise from site-owned errors. Request the broken module URL directly and compare it to its filesystem source.

### 3. Close The Dependency Graph

Read the complete `/apps` entry surface and recursively trace imports, HTML references, CSS assets, foundation modules, favicons, import maps, service workers, and URL helpers. Search Git history for recent path changes.

### 4. Locate Systemic Ownership

Trace static serving, API route precedence, MIME assignment, fallback behavior, redirects, and caching. Only then decide whether the root cause belongs to `/apps`, shared browser libraries, or the server.

### 5. Discover The Whole Page Surface

Enumerate actual page entrypoints and safe dynamic fixtures. Reuse existing crawler/runtime tools if adequate; otherwise add focused small modules for route discovery, dependency checks, runtime observation, and reporting.

### 6. Repair In Dependency Order

Systemic routing/static failures first, then shared API transport/contracts, then shared UI primitives, then page-local defects. Keep public compatibility unless every consumer migrates together.

### 7. Make The UI Cinematic Without Making It Fragile

Use scoped/local selectors, coherent tokens, responsive layouts, strong readable focus, controlled motion, reduced-motion alternatives, stable overlays, intentional media sizing, safe-area behavior, and complete loading/empty/error states. Verify representative viewports rather than styling from intuition.

### 8. Make APIs More Realistic

Where evidence supports it, normalize transport errors, content-type handling, abort semantics, request races, validation, permissions, and endpoint adapters. Prefer small data-driven modules to sprawling conditional code. Do not invent incompatible response envelopes merely to look organized.

### 9. Verify More Aggressively Than We Write

Run syntax/import checks, existing tests, new root-cause regressions, static-reference audits, runtime crawls, viewport checks, and direct endpoint/module probes. Re-read every touched file and compare plan versus implementation.

### 10. Publish With Provenance

Review every changed file, classify unrelated work, exclude secret/local-only hazards, commit the safe complete tree requested by the user, push the canonical branch, observe the actual deployment mechanism, verify remote HEAD, then crawl the canonical live URL independently of localhost.

## Final Completion Invariant

`REMAINING_WORK` becomes empty only when source, tests, runtime, Git, remote, deployment, and live-host evidence all agree. A passing local page is not a deployed page. A successful push is not a verified deployment. A visually correct page is not a runtime-clean page. Every layer must testify.
